cards.text: Remember Stephen, the believer who was stoned (Acts 7:59)? A persecution began with him, and the believers scattered as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch. And everywhere they go, they're sharing the message.

cards.question: At first, the scattered believers speak the message only to ___.

cards.text: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, get to Antioch and open the door WIDE. They're the one coworker who invites the whole building to the party, not just his department.

cards.question: In Antioch, what do the men from Cyprus and Cyrene start doing?

answers.text: Telling the Greeks about Jesus too
Telling the Romans about Jesus too
Telling the Egyptians about Jesus too

cards.text: We never even get these guys' names, and I had mine CARVED into my handle and still ended up in a junk drawer. Doesn't matter, because the hand of the Lord is with them.

cards.question: Only a handful of people in Antioch believe and turn to the Lord.

cards.text: A GREAT number. That's not a small group anymore, that's a stadium, and the news reaches the ears of the church in Jerusalem.

cards.question: When the church in Jerusalem hears what's happening, they send ___ to Antioch.

cards.text: Barnabas is a believer from Cyprus who once sold a field and brought the money to the apostles (Acts 4:36-37). He arrives in Antioch, looks around, and sees the grace of God.

cards.question: When Barnabas sees the grace of God in Antioch, he's troubled by it.

cards.text: He rejoices. His name means Son of Encouragement (Acts 4:36), and the man is about to go out and LIVE his name tag.

cards.question: Barnabas encourages all the believers in Antioch to do what?

answers.text: Abide in the Lord with all their hearts
Go back to Jerusalem with him
Wait for the apostles to come

cards.question: Acts calls Barnabas a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. With him there in Antioch, a great number of people are brought to the Lord.

cards.text: Then Barnabas heads to Tarsus to look for somebody. No phone, no GPS, just a whole city and one name, and that's COMMITMENT, friend.

cards.question: Who is Barnabas looking for in Tarsus?

cards.text: Saul is the man who once breathed threats against believers until Jesus stopped him on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:1-6). Barnabas finds him and brings him back to Antioch.

cards.question: Barnabas and Saul stay in Antioch only a few days before moving on.

cards.text: A full YEAR meeting with the church and teaching large numbers of people. That's not a visit, friend. That's a lease.

cards.question: At Antioch, the disciples are first called ___.

cards.text: In those days, some prophets come down from Jerusalem to Antioch. One of them, Agabus, stands up and predicts through the Spirit what's coming, and it's not good news.

cards.question: What does Agabus predict will sweep across the whole world?

cards.text: And it really happens, under Claudius, the Roman emperor. Most folks hear news like that and start hiding cookies in the back of the cupboard, but watch these disciples.

cards.question: The disciples in Antioch decide to send relief to the brothers living in ___.
The disciples in Antioch all agree to give the exact same amount.
Who carries the Antioch disciples' gifts to the elders?

findings.problem: "Remember Stephen...?" assumes the baker already knows Stephen from an earlier lesson. Papa Dorin isn't told how far the baker has gone. The card should introduce Stephen without assuming the baker remembers him.

rule.text: What he doesn't know: anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't land right away. It sets the unnamed men against Papa Dorin, who had his name carved and still got forgotten, and then says "Doesn't matter." The comparison doesn't share one clear action with the moment, so an adult has to work out what the point is.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Abide in the Lord with all their hearts," uses Bible wording. The wrong answers, "Go back to Jerusalem with him" and "Wait for the apostles to come," are plain modern phrasing. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The setup card only says Agabus predicts something that is "not good news." A famine, a flood and a plague all fit that, so nothing earlier helps the baker reason to famine, and the pick comes down to luck. The passage already has several discovery questions (Greeks, Barnabas, Saul), so this one should be made reasonable to work out.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card calls Claudius "the Roman emperor." That fact comes from outside Acts 11:28 and has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.
